# E039 -- Pratt Institute Brand Guidelines

## Metadata
- **Company:** Pratt Institute
- **Industry:** Education
- **Year:** 2022
- **Source file:** pratt-v2-pdf.pdf
- **Pages:** 67
- **Language:** EN
- **Pages sampled:** 1-2, 6-7, 12-13

## Brand Strategy
- Titled "Identity Guidelines" -- V2, dated November 2022
- Philosophy: the Pratt name and reputation anchor diverse parts; the parts give breadth/depth to the name -- symbiotic relationship
- Unlike previous identity systems, this refresh provides flexible guidelines and tools alongside clear requirements
- Iconic Pratt logo remains unchanged; sub-brand architecture expanded and clarified
- New typefaces introduced for greater flexibility; expanded secondary and tertiary color palettes
- Goal: communication designs that are "at once unique and recognizably Pratt"

## Logo
- Iconic Pratt logo remains unchanged from previous identity system
- Logo lockups at primary or secondary scale
- Sub-brand architecture: departments, schools, centers each have logo lockup variants under Pratt umbrella

## Typography
- **Graphik** (normal width) -- primary sans-serif
- **Tiempos Text** -- body serif
- **Tiempos Headline** -- display serif for headlines
- **Tiempos Fine** -- used in optical size-specific situations
- Administration (fixed end of spectrum): Graphik Normal + Tiempos only
- More flexible categories (Academics, Centers, Student Groups) may have broader type options

## Color
- Primary color palette required for Administration (fixed end of spectrum)
- Color selection becomes progressively more open along the flexibility spectrum
- Student groups: color selection is "open and unrestricted"
- Expanded secondary and tertiary color palettes introduced in this refresh (details likely on later pages)

## Graphics
- "Frame and content" system: fixed elements (frame) + variable elements (content)
- Frame = standardized identifiers and informative structures across communications
- Content = flexible elements placed within the frame per user/entity/audience needs
- Visual identity composed of fixed elements (logo) and variable elements (color, typography, layout)

## Photography
- Not covered in sampled pages

## Applications
- Stationery and business cards, campus signage, website (Pratt.edu), intranet
- Development/fundraising materials, admissions materials
- On-campus posters and social media
- Group/initiative-specific visual identities and publications (e.g., Prattonia, The Prattler)

## Tone of Voice
- Not explicitly covered in sampled pages; emphasis is on visual identity system

## Outliers
- **Flexibility spectrum** is a distinctive framework -- continuum from "Fixed" (Administration) to "Flexible" (Student Groups), with Academics, Events, Resources, Centers in between
- 67-page document is unusually thorough for an educational institution
- Graphik typeface family includes extremely rare widths: Compact, Wide, Condensed, XCond, XXCond, XXXCond, XXXXCond, and Produkt variants
- Explicitly allows student groups to use non-Pratt typefaces and unrestricted color -- uncommon openness in brand guidelines

## Quality Score
- **4/5** -- Comprehensive, well-structured identity system with a sophisticated flexibility spectrum framework; thorough sub-brand architecture; only slightly below 5 due to limited photography and tone-of-voice coverage in sampled pages
